title: Access Moodle with the mobile app
content:
Use this procedure for the Moodle mobile app. It is separate from browser access through MCeLE.

### App access

1. Log in to MCeLE with your username and password.
2. Use your MCeLE username, not your email; it is normally `firstname.middleinitial.lastname`, such as `john.a.doe`. The username is not case sensitive.
3. In MCeLE, select **Instructor-Led Courses** in the left navigation menu to activate your Moodle account.
4. Download the Moodle app from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store.
5. In the app, enter the exact, case-sensitive site URL `elearning.mcele.usmc.mil/moodle`.
6. Select **Log in**.
7. Log in with your MCeLE username and password.
8. When prompted to **Open this page in Moodle**, select **Open**.
9. Confirm that you return to the Dashboard in the Moodle app.

### QR code enrollment

1. In the Moodle app, select the three dots in the bottom-right navigation bar.
2. Select **Scan QR Code**.
3. Scan the QR code provided for the course.
If there is a problem, contact the Student Support Help Desk and use **option 3 for Moodle support**.

### Locked out

1. Close every open window and tab.
2. Open a new session and retry.
3. If the same error remains, contact the Help Desk at **1-888-435-8762** and use **option 3 for Moodle support**.

### Moodle support

For persistent app access or login problems, contact the **Student Support Help Desk** and use **option 3 for Moodle support**.

Use the same option 3 escalation if a Moodle course tile is missing, a course material or activity will not open, an Instructor or Adjunct Faculty member has a problem with a Moodle course in which they are a participant, or an Academics Officer has a problem with a Moodle course or activity they created.

provenance.description: Adapted from the approved Confluence Moodle-app article, preserving its MCeLE activation, app setup, exact case-sensitive site URL, return-to-app, QR-code, and source Help Desk instructions. User-confirmed Moodle support escalation was added for persistent app access and uncovered course or activity problems.
